chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said: I asked him about a man who gives from his zakat dirhams in exchange for dinars, and dinars in exchange for dirhams, at the current value. Is that permissible for him? He said, 'There is no harm.'
The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And it is not permissible to pay the value in the zakat of livestock unless the specific animals designated for zakat are unavailable.

7 - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Muqarrin ibn Abdullah ibn Zam'a, from his father, from his grandfather's father: That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) wrote to him in a letter which he wrote with his own hand when he sent him to collect the charity (zakat).

'Whoever has among his camels the zakat due is a jadha'ah (five-year-old female camel), but he does not have a jadha'ah and instead has a hiqqah (four-year-old female camel), then the hiqqah is accepted from him, and two sheep or twenty dirhams are given with it.

And whoever has among his camels the zakat due is a hiqqah, but he does not have a hiqqah and instead has a jadha'ah, then the jadha'ah is accepted from him, and the collector gives him two sheep or twenty dirhams.

And whoever's zakat is a hiqqah, but he does not have a hiqqah and instead has a ibnath labun (three-year-old female camel), then he is accepted from him, and he gives with it two sheep or twenty dirhams.
And whoever's zakat is an ibnath labun, but he does not have an ibnath labun and instead has a hiqqah, then the hiqqah is accepted from him, and the collector gives him two sheep or twenty dirhams.

And whoever's zakat is an ibnath labun, but he does not have an ibnath labun and instead has an ibnath makhidh (two-year-old female camel), then the ibnath makhidh is accepted from him, and he gives with it two sheep or twenty dirhams.

And whoever's zakat is an ibnath makhidh, but he does not have an ibnath makhidh and instead has an ibnath labun, then the ibnath labun is accepted from him, and the collector gives him two sheep or twenty dirhams.

And whoever does not have an ibnath makhidh in its proper condition and instead has a male ibn labun (male three-year-old camel), then the male ibn labun is accepted from him, and there is nothing given with it.
And whoever has only four camels and no other wealth, then there is no zakat in them unless the owner wishes. When his wealth reaches five camels, then in them is one sheep.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for paying zakat on livestock if the specific required animal is not available?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'iqab' (compensation) in zakat, allowing the substitution of specific livestock categories when the primary obligation is unavailable, a rule later codified by scholars like Al-Tusi. It highlights the flexibility within Shia fiqh to ensure the fulfillment of religious duty without undue hardship, specifying that the collector (musaddiq) provides two sheep or twenty dirhams as compensation for the deviation from the exact prescribed animal. This mechanism underscores the practical application of Quranic injunctions on charity, ensuring equitable distribution even when specific assets are lacking.
